title: Optimality of the greedy edge-selection sweep
statement: Let $\mathit{edges}$ be a list of weighted edges on $n$ vertices, sorted in nondecreasing order of weight, and let $\mathit{uf}$ be a union-find state whose induced partition is exactly the reachability relation of some base edge list $\mathit{base}$: for all vertices $a$ and $b$, the representatives $\mathit{uf}(a)$ and $\mathit{uf}(b)$ are equal if and only if $a$ and $b$ are joined by a path through the edges of $\mathit{base}$. Let $S$ be any list of edges, each of which occurs in $\mathit{edges}$, such that merging all of $S$ into $\mathit{uf}$ and merging all of $\mathit{edges}$ into $\mathit{uf}$ yield the same partition of the vertices. Then the greedy sweep — which starts from $\mathit{uf}$, scans $\mathit{edges}$ in order, and keeps each edge exactly when its two endpoints lie in currently distinct components — produces a set of edges whose total weight is at most the total weight of $S$.
hypotheses_covered: uf's partition equals the reachability relation of the base edge list
every edge of S occurs in edges
merging S into uf gives the same partition as merging all of edges into uf
edges is sorted in nondecreasing order of weight
replaced:
Let $uf$ be a union--find state whose classes are exactly the reachability classes of a
base edge list, and let the input list $edges$ be sorted by nondecreasing weight. Then
for any competing sublist $S \subseteq edges$ that induces the same partition as $edges$
does over $uf$, the greedy output satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{totalWeight}\bigl(\mathrm{processEdges}\;edges\;uf\;[\,]\bigr)
  \;\le\; \mathrm{totalWeight}(S).
\]
